interpretations.statement: Across recorded nominal executions the holding tip-speed weight is not monotonically related to holding maximum speed (0.06, 0.075 and 0.1 nominal points exceeded the 0.02 m/s limit, while 0.05 and 0.09 passed), so no monotone control direction may be assumed for the perturbation.

plan.hypothesis: At the frozen near_z_plus initial-angle/rate perturbation (seed 17) the unchanged incumbent control weights (holding 0.05, terminal 0.05) remain jointly reach-and-hold accepted, whereas raising the holding tip-speed weight to 0.09 with terminal weight 0.1 lowers holding maximum speed relative to the perturbed reference without restoring joint acceptance by a design edit; control-weight adaptation is the affordable direction for perturbation robustness.
plan.rationale: Goal: separate the frozen perturbation from the confounded changed-structure failure by measuring the unchanged incumbent as a perturbed reference and one affordable control probe. Method: search.family_explicit@1.0.0 with two exact enumerated points and null step, so each point rebuilds all selected values and runs one unchanged stable-v7 closed loop; no inner adaptation search. Assumptions and limits: no continuity, monotonicity or interpolation of the (holding weight, terminal weight) to (holding speed, holding position error) map is assumed; a passing reference does not prove broad robustness; a lower holding speed with higher position error is a trade-off, not overall improvement; the incumbent is not claimed to have the best speed margin. Allocation: 2 backend attempts (limit 2), case near_z_plus, seed 17, both points sharing the batch. Expected information: (a) whether the unchanged incumbent is jointly accepted at the frozen perturbation, (b) whether a higher holding weight changes perturbed holding speed jointly with the three physical metrics. Exit: complete profile of both points, with per-point acceptance and physical metrics reported separately.
stopping_conditions: Both candidates reach complete profiled evaluation and bound_comparison, then stop.
weakening_observations: F118 incumbent holding_max_speed 0.012750255515948416 m/s is not the lowest observed (0.010201160469407439 m/s at holding/terminal 0.09/0.1 and 0.01273567785134029 m/s at holding 0.0), so no global best-margin claim and no guaranteed speed gain is made.

The proposed 0.09/0.1 point already showed a trade-off at nominal (holding 0.003370231014572803 m vs incumbent 0.0027300544346297905 m with terminal error 0.0033130137577230853 m vs 0.002697828858325615 m): lower speed with worse position error.

Nominal holding-weight 0.1 (110dc2c9c1d642dcb018664a65c62c30, 0.022128674933740447 m/s), 0.06 (312ef97407b34ff28905e883a947f475, 0.023994623331658485 m/s) and 0.075 (e3876a1d289f41f08d46c96202f1da0c, 0.023285947509969908 m/s) all failed, contradicting a monotone weight-versus-speed expectation.
Candidate 0 repeats the known incumbent weights; it is a first-time reference at this case, not scientific novelty, and cannot alone establish robustness.
The near_z_plus holding-speed failure of the changed-section candidate (F4) cannot be used to screen out either control point.

arguments.reasoning: The one current direct datum on the frozen perturbation is a changed near-section-scale candidate at near_z_plus (F3 valid_failure, F51 accepted=false, F45 holding-speed fail at F4=0.06758272073425946 m/s vs 0.02 limit). That failure is confounded: it belongs to a changed structure plus the perturbation, so it does not establish the unchanged incumbent's perturbed behavior, which the frozen question explicitly names as the gap. The retained incumbent is accepted only at nominal (F123 true, F14 accepted) with F24=0.002697828858325615 m, F116=0.0027300544346297905 m, F118=0.012750255515948416 m/s. Local affine/nominal-only evidence cannot guarantee nonlinear reach, braking or perturbation robustness, and sealed M5 negative forecasts have no screening authority, so a small measured control batch is the cheapest decisive step. I therefore propose one immutable 2-point explicit control batch at near_z_plus seed 17: (1) the unchanged incumbent weights (0.05, 0.05) as a perturbed reference — the first execution of that configuration at this case, a reference not a novelty and not by itself a robustness claim; (2) a higher holding tip-speed weight (0.09, 0.1), the one recorded nominal point that passed (148a2a290daa440f9b966f4d5cee4b5f) while showing lower holding speed (0.010201160469407439 m/s) but higher holding position error (0.003370231014572803 m) — i.e., an expected trade-off, not overall improvement. Explicit points are enumerated, never interpolated, and are not an optimization; no monotonicity of the weight-to-speed map is assumed (nominal holding weights 0.06/0.075/0.1 exceeded 0.02 m/s while 0.05 and 0.09 passed). I also decline to claim the incumbent holds the globally best speed margin (0.010201160469407439 and 0.01273567785134029 are lower). Cost: 2 new backend attempts (limit 2), 1 case, 1 seed; no inner adaptation search.
